title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Network. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Network
options.lineage: Transit wayfinding: Unimark-era signage, strip maps, departures boards
options.thesis: Your life as a transit network: writing, reading, travel, work and music are lines, and every essay, book, trip and set is a stop on one.
options.viewport: One strip map runs down the home page with five coloured lines, each naming its next stop (latest essay, current book, last trip, what you're building, the set), beside a small departures board on your local clock.
options.risk: Turns into a gimmick if stops are forced; every line must still read as a plain list without the map.

raised.raise: One vertical axis rules the home page: a single strip map, with every item hanging off its line.
Locked palette: index thumbnails are printed as duotones in their line's colour, so mixed trip photos read as one set.
A mark system: each line's bullet heads every page on that line, so you always know where you are.
Photos arrive with one develop-in reveal, used only there, not scattered effects.
One module, the line's stroke width, sets every gap and alignment on the site.

options.label: Liner Notes
options.lineage: Record sleeves, centre labels and liner notes from a DJ's crate
options.thesis: The site as a record you're holding: your SoundCloud set is the record on the platter, essays are sleeves in the crate, and the reading list is what's in your bag.
options.viewport: Your name set as an album sleeve with a tracklist of what you're doing now. The Blender turntable sits beside it, and pressing play spins the set.
options.risk: Familiar music-portfolio territory, and it gets cute if essays are forced into tracks. This is also where many personal sites with a music angle land.

options.label: Source Floor
options.lineage: Algorave: live-coded music projected over a dance floor
options.thesis: Engineer and DJ in one buffer: each section is a running pattern, and the set plays as the code ticks.
options.viewport: A full-screen code buffer whose lines are your sections, with the set's waveform keeping time.
options.case: It holds audience identification, since you're both engineer and DJ, but loses on clarity: essays, books and trips don't live naturally in a code buffer.
options.risk: A terminal look is the tech-site default, and the shared clock is what's worth keeping.

options.label: Safelight
options.lineage: A photo printing darkroom under amber light
options.thesis: Everything develops slowly, like a print in the tray.
options.viewport: Trip prints emerging under amber light.
options.case: Good for photos, but essays and reading don't belong in a darkroom.

options.label: Sixteen Colours
options.thesis: A fixed frame where only the contents change.
options.viewport: A dithered portrait with a text window docked low.
options.case: Retro novelty with nothing tying it to you.
options.kept: A locked palette that every image is rendered through.

options.label: Deep Dive
options.lineage: A technical dive down a reef wall
options.case: Beautiful, but nothing in your life maps to depth.
options.kept: One vertical axis that rules every line of the page.

options.label: Woodcut Sun
options.viewport: A woodcut mark over torn paper.
options.case: Pastiche; it says nothing about an engineer.
options.kept: A mark per section that stamps the header.

options.label: Build Steps
options.thesis: Numbered steps on a stud grid.
options.case: Instructional; a personal site isn't a sequence.
options.kept: One module unit governing all alignment.

canonCard.label: Quiet personal index
canonCard.thesis: The category standard, done carefully: one column, one voice, plain lists, a small now block, photos in a calm grid.
canonCard.viewport: Name and a two-line bio, then Now, Writing, Reading, Places, and the set as short lists.
canonCard.risk: Clean and forgettable; the room most likely goes.
